title: Ukraine Lost in Bakhmut. But It Has Much Bigger Plans.

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏品去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: Before we get started today, I wanted to share two pieces of exciting news.
sentences.zh: 在今天开始之前，我想分享两个令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.en: The first is that we here at New York Times Audio have just released an app.
sentences.zh: 第一个是，我们《纽约时报》音频部门刚刚发布了一款应用程序。

sentences.en: For fans of New York Times podcasts like you, it does something very helpful.
sentences.zh: 对于像你这样的《纽约时报》播客粉丝来说，它非常实用。

sentences.en: It takes all kinds of shows like Serial, The Run-Up, This American Life, The Daily, and gathers them into one place.
sentences.zh: 它汇集了《Serial》、《The Run-Up》、《This American Life》、《The Daily》等各类节目，将它们整合在一个地方。

sentences.en: And it helps you discover the new shows that we're making that you might not know about.
sentences.zh: 它还能帮你发现我们制作的、你可能还不知道的新节目。

sentences.en: And that brings me to the second piece of exciting news, which is that New York Times Audio is launching a new news show.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了第二个令人兴奋的消息，那就是《纽约时报》音频部门正在推出一档新的新闻节目。

sentences.en: It's called The Headlines.
sentences.zh: 它叫《头条新闻》（The Headlines）。

sentences.en: As a daily listener, you know that what we do every day is we bring you one story in depth.
sentences.zh: 作为每日听众，你知道我们每天都在为你深入报道一个故事。

sentences.en: But of course, our newsroom is covering dozens and dozens of stories every single day.
sentences.zh: 但当然，我们的新闻编辑室每天都在报道几十个故事。

sentences.en: And that's what The Headlines is for.
sentences.zh: 这就是《头条新闻》的意义所在。

sentences.en: It's a short show that brings you the top stories of the day straight from the reporters covering them.
sentences.zh: 这是一档简短的节目，直接由负责报道的记者为你带来当天的头条新闻。

sentences.en: This week, we're sending the show right down our feed for you to listen to.
sentences.zh: 本周，我们会将该节目直接推送到你的订阅源中，供你收听。

sentences.en: And after that, you can find it on our app.
sentences.zh: 之后，你可以在我们的应用程序上找到它。

sentences.en: Search NYT Audio in the App Store or go to nytimes.com slash audio app.
sentences.zh: 在应用商店搜索“NYT Audio”或访问 nytimes.com/audioapp。

sentences.en: Everything in there is available to all New York Times subscribers.
sentences.zh: 其中的所有内容都向《纽约时报》的所有订阅者开放。

sentences.en: We hope you'll check it out.
sentences.zh: 希望你会去看看。

sentences.en: Okay, now here's today's show.
sentences.zh: 好了，现在是今天的节目。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: And this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》（The Daily）。

sentences.en: After almost a year of fighting, Russia finally captured Bakhmut, a city in eastern Ukraine, with Moscow declaring it a mission accomplished moment.
sentences.zh: 经过近一年的战斗，俄罗斯终于占领了乌克兰东部的巴赫穆特，莫斯科宣布这是一次“任务达成”。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Eric Schmidt explains what the capture really means and why the next few months for Ukraine are so critical.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事埃里克·施密特将解释这次占领的真正含义，以及为什么接下来的几个月对乌克兰如此关键。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, May 24th.
sentences.zh: 今天是5月24日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Eric, you and I and all of our colleagues have been watching this one city in eastern Ukraine, Bakhmut.
sentences.zh: 埃里克，你、我和我们所有的同事一直在关注乌克兰东部的这座城市——巴赫穆特。

sentences.en: It's literally been the focal point of the war over the past many months.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几个月里，它实际上一直是战争的焦点。

sentences.en: And finally, over the weekend, it fell.
sentences.zh: 最终，在周末，它陷落了。

sentences.en: Bakhmut fell to the Russians.
sentences.zh: 巴赫穆特落入了俄罗斯人手中。

sentences.en: How important is this?
sentences.zh: 这有多重要？

sentences.en: Well, you have to remember what kind of came before this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你得记住之前发生了什么。

sentences.en: Obviously, the Russians failed in their initial attempt.
sentences.zh: 显然，俄罗斯人在最初的尝试中失败了。

sentences.en: They were driven out of Kiev.
sentences.zh: 他们被赶出了基辅。

sentences.en: They then resumed last summer in the fighting in the Donbass.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，他们随后在顿巴斯地区恢复了战斗。

sentences.en: Then they suffered some other defeats in places called Kharkiv and Kherson in the southern part of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 之后，他们在乌克兰南部的哈尔科夫和赫尔松遭遇了一些失败。

sentences.en: So by late last summer, the Russians were looking for a victory.
sentences.zh: 所以到去年夏末，俄罗斯人急需一场胜利。

sentences.en: Tonight, new details from the front lines of Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 今晚，来自乌克兰前线的最新消息。

sentences.en: The Russian-appointed leader in Ukraine's Donetsk region now claims that Russian forces are closing in around the city of Bakhmut.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯任命的乌克兰顿涅茨克地区领导人声称，俄军正在包围巴赫穆特市。

sentences.en: And they identified this city of about 75,000 people, Bakhmut, as a place where if they could take that, they felt they could expand their presence in the Donbass.
sentences.zh: 他们将这座约有7.5万人口的城市巴赫穆特视为一个目标，如果能拿下它，他们认为就能扩大在顿巴斯的存在。

sentences.en: The city became a key target for Russian forces after they were forced to withdraw from other areas of the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 在被迫从东部其他地区撤出后，这座城市成为了俄军的关键目标。

sentences.en: And so they began focusing their attack on this city.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始集中力量攻击这座城市。

sentences.en: There is little strategic value.
sentences.zh: 它几乎没有什么战略价值。

sentences.en: It's not a military hub.
sentences.zh: 它不是军事枢纽。

sentences.en: It's not a communications hub or a transport hub.
sentences.zh: 它也不是通信枢纽或交通枢纽。

sentences.en: But that said, Russia has had very few victories for quite a long time in this conflict.
sentences.zh: 但话虽如此，俄罗斯在这场冲突中已经很久没有取得什么胜利了。

sentences.en: And so any seizure or capture of part or most of Bakhmut would be seen as a success, as a victory by the...
sentences.zh: 因此，任何对巴赫穆特部分或大部分地区的夺取或占领，都会被视为一种成功，被视为一场胜利……

sentences.en: And for the most part, I think people thought, well, that's going to be probably given the Russian wherewithal.
sentences.zh: 而且在很大程度上，我认为人们觉得，考虑到俄罗斯的财力物力，这大概是……

sentences.en: They would probably be able to take that city fairly easily.
sentences.zh: 他们大概能相当容易地拿下那座城市。

sentences.en: Russian and Ukrainian forces are still fighting in the streets of Bakhmut, which Russia has been trying to capture for several months.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯和乌克兰军队仍在巴赫穆特的街道上战斗，俄罗斯已经试图占领该市好几个月了。

sentences.en: Thousands of Russian troops have died trying to take the eastern city.
sentences.zh: 数千名俄罗斯士兵在试图夺取这座东部城市时丧生。

sentences.en: But what happened was the Ukrainians decided, hey, you know, we're going to make more of an investment in this.
sentences.zh: 但实际情况是，乌克兰人决定，嘿，你知道吗，我们要在这上面投入更多。

sentences.en: If this is so important to Russia that they win, at least have a symbolic victory, if not an actual military victory,
sentences.zh: 如果俄罗斯如此渴望获胜，至少要取得一场象征性的胜利，如果不是实际的军事胜利的话，

sentences.en: we're going to stand in their way and we're going to hang on as long as we can to block the Russians from achieving that triumph.
sentences.zh: 我们就要挡在他们面前，尽我们所能坚持下去，阻止俄罗斯人实现那个目标。

sentences.en: Okay, so this is kind of a strategically unimportant place that for some reason became important.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以这本来是一个战略上不重要的地方，却因为某种原因变得重要起来了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Think of it almost as if two dogs fighting over a bone here.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它想象成两只狗在争抢一根骨头。

sentences.en: One is much larger and should have yanked this bone away a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 其中一只大得多，本应早就把骨头抢走了。

sentences.en: But the smaller dog is hanging on for dear life and denying the bigger dog the bone.
sentences.zh: 但较小的那只狗拼死不放，不让大狗得到骨头。

sentences.en: That's kind of what's happening here and that because Bakhmut is so important for the Russians, the Ukrainians are hanging on.
sentences.zh: 这就是现在发生的事情，因为巴赫穆特对俄罗斯人来说太重要了，所以乌克兰人一直在坚持。

sentences.en: And by March, American officials are kind of saying to the Ukrainians, you know, hey, aren't you worried here that you could be wasting too much manpower and resources
sentences.zh: 到了三月，美国官员开始对乌克兰人说，嘿，你们不担心吗？你们可能会浪费太多人力和资源，

sentences.en: that you're going to need for future fights that are much more important to this larger campaign than this place Bakhmut?
sentences.zh: 而这些资源是你们在未来战斗中需要的，那些战斗对这场更大规模的战役来说比巴赫穆特这个地方重要得多。

sentences.en: But the Ukrainians say, no, we're going to hang on here because anything that can deny Putin a victory is in of itself a political victory for us, the underdog,
sentences.zh: 但乌克兰人说，不，我们要在这里坚持下去，因为任何能让普京无法获胜的事情，对于我们这些弱势方来说，本身就是一场政治胜利，

sentences.en: just as it's been for months and months now as we've pushed back on the Russians before.
sentences.zh: 就像过去几个月我们一直抵御俄罗斯人时一样。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then over the weekend, of course, as we know, Bakhmut falls.
sentences.zh: 然后到了周末，正如我们所知，巴赫穆特陷落了。

sentences.en: The Russians take it.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人占领了它。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Russians declared basically mission accomplished.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人基本上宣布任务达成。

sentences.en: The city is essentially a wasteland, although the Ukrainians are still fighting from outside the city.
sentences.zh: 这座城市基本上已经是一片废墟，尽管乌克兰人仍在城外进行战斗。

sentences.en: So it's not completely over yet.
sentences.zh: 所以还没有完全结束。

sentences.en: But what's really important here is what happens in the kind of critical next phase of the war.
sentences.zh: 但真正重要的是战争接下来的关键阶段会发生什么。

sentences.en: The battle over Bakhmut might actually turn out to be a very smart strategy by the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 巴赫穆特之战实际上可能被证明是乌克兰人的一项非常聪明的策略。

sentences.en: A smart strategy.
sentences.zh: 聪明的策略。

sentences.en: But why would it be a smart strategy?
sentences.zh: 但为什么会是聪明的策略呢？

sentences.en: I mean, this is essentially the Ukrainians losing territory, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这本质上是乌克兰人在失去领土，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a loss for the Ukrainians.
sentences.zh: 这对乌克兰人来说是一次损失。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But go back and remember why the Ukrainians have been fighting over this for the last several months.
sentences.zh: 但回过头来想想，为什么乌克兰人在过去几个月里一直为此战斗。

sentences.en: Anyway, their idea has been pin down as many Russian forces in this otherwise not as very important place for as long as possible.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他们的想法是尽可能长时间地在这个本来没那么重要的地方牵制住尽可能多的俄军。

sentences.en: Kill and injure as many Russian forces as you can.
sentences.zh: 尽可能多地杀伤俄军。

sentences.en: In fact, the United States says as many as 100,000 Russians have either died or been injured since January, mostly in and around Bakhmut.
sentences.zh: 事实上，美国称自一月以来，多达10万名俄罗斯人伤亡，大部分是在巴赫穆特及其周边地区。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's more than the population of Bakhmut.
sentences.zh: 那比巴赫穆特的人口还要多。

sentences.en: I mean, that is just an unbelievable number.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这简直是一个令人难以置信的数字。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And perhaps most important, it's buying time for the Ukrainians to build up this major force,
sentences.zh: 也许最重要的是，这为乌克兰人争取了时间来建立这支主力部队，

sentences.en: this big arsenal of weapons and newly trained soldiers that will mount a counteroffensive.
sentences.zh: 这支拥有大量武器和新训练士兵的庞大军力，将发动反攻。

sentences.en: Their first really big push since last fall to take back territory that the Russians hold.
sentences.zh: 这是他们自去年秋天以来真正意义上的第一次大动作，旨在夺回被俄罗斯人占领的领土。

sentences.en: It's a counteroffensive that we believe is probably going to start as early as June.
sentences.zh: 这是一场我们认为很可能最早在六月开始的反攻。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The counteroffensive.
sentences.zh: 反攻。

sentences.en: Also known as the spring offensive.
sentences.zh: 也被称为春季攻势。

sentences.en: Something that people who've been following this war closely, like you and I have, have been expecting for months.
sentences.zh: 像你我这样密切关注这场战争的人，几个月来一直都在期待着。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And spring, because the mud season is more or less over and the ground is hard enough for large military vehicles to drive on.
sentences.zh: 之所以叫春季攻势，是因为泥泞季节差不多结束了，地面足够坚硬，可以让大型军用车辆行驶。

sentences.en: So people watching the war have pegged this time as the chance for a major counteroffensive by Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 所以观察这场战争的人们将这段时间定为乌克兰进行大规模反攻的机会。

sentences.en: And tell us, Eric, when did the planning for it begin?
sentences.zh: 告诉我们，埃里克，计划是什么时候开始的？

sentences.en: The planning began almost within weeks after the last major offensive that the Ukrainians carried out last fall in Harasson.
sentences.zh: 计划几乎是在乌克兰人去年秋天在赫尔松进行上一次大反攻后的几周内就开始了。

sentences.en: They start planning.
sentences.zh: 他们开始规划。

sentences.en: How are they going to amass a big enough force to drive out the Russians from the remaining territory that they still hold?
sentences.zh: 他们将如何集结足够强大的力量，将俄罗斯人从他们仍然占领的剩余领土上赶走？

sentences.en: And so Zelensky starts, you know, going around and oppressing the Western allies for munitions.
sentences.zh: 于是泽连斯基开始四处奔走，向西方盟友寻求弹药。

sentences.en: It's a great honor for me to be at the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我非常荣幸能来到美国国会，

sentences.en: Congress and speak to you and all Americans.
sentences.zh: 向你们和所有美国人发表讲话。

sentences.en: Remember back in December, he visits the United States, leaving Ukraine for the first time during the war,
sentences.zh: 还记得去年十二月，他访问美国，这是他在战争期间第一次离开乌克兰，

sentences.en: to drum up support for things like the Patriot missile batteries, for the Abrams tanks, both systems that the United States was initially reluctant to provide.
sentences.zh: 为“爱国者”导弹系统、艾布拉姆斯坦克等装备争取支持，这两套系统美国最初都不愿提供。

sentences.en: We have artillery.
sentences.zh: 我们有火炮。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We have it.
sentences.zh: 我们有。

sentences.en: Is it enough?
sentences.zh: 够吗？

sentences.en: Honestly, not really.
sentences.zh: 老实说，不够。

sentences.en: And then most recently, just in the last week or so, he went on a global tour.
sentences.zh: 然后最近，就在过去一周左右，他进行了一次全球巡访。

sentences.en: Ukrainian President Zelensky's diplomatic tour across Europe, all this coming as Ukraine's long-anticipated spring counteroffensive could be starting.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰总统泽连斯基在欧洲的外交巡访，这一切都发生在乌克兰期待已久的春季反攻可能即将开始之际。

sentences.en: He went to Germany and got nearly $3 billion.
sentences.zh: 他去了德国，获得了近30亿美元的援助。

sentences.en: It's the biggest package of military aid that Germany's offered Ukraine since this conflict started, and it includes 30 Leopard tanks, 15 anti-aircraft tanks, more than 200.
sentences.zh: 这是自冲突开始以来德国向乌克兰提供的最大一笔军事援助，其中包括30辆豹式坦克、15辆防空坦克，以及超过200枚……

sentences.en: He went to Britain.
sentences.zh: 他去了英国。

sentences.en: Rishi Sunak's office saying new equipment for Ukraine would include hundreds of long-range attack drones.
sentences.zh: 里希·苏纳克的办公室表示，为乌克兰提供的新装备将包括数百架远程攻击无人机。

sentences.en: Last week, Britain sent...
sentences.zh: 上周，英国派遣了……

sentences.en: And finally, he ended up at the G7 summit in Japan.
sentences.zh: 最后，他参加了在日本举行的七国集团（G7）峰会。

sentences.en: Washington confirmed that it has given the green light to training on much longed-for combat jets.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿证实，已为训练乌克兰飞行员驾驶梦寐以求的战斗机开了绿灯。

sentences.en: Where he, for the first time, was able to get commitments from the United States to allow Ukrainian pilots to train in American-made F-16 fighter jets.
sentences.zh: 在那里，他第一次获得了美国的承诺，允许乌克兰飞行员接受美制F-16战斗机的训练。

sentences.en: And for the United States to allow European countries that own F-16s to transfer those important fighter jets to Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 并允许拥有F-16的欧洲国家将这些重要的战斗机转让给乌克兰。

sentences.en: And it's followed a similar pattern to what we've seen with other requests for advanced weapons.
sentences.zh: 这遵循了我们之前在其他先进武器请求中看到的类似模式。

sentences.en: That first the Allies say no, and then they say maybe, and then they finally get to yes.
sentences.zh: 盟友们先是说不，然后说可能，最后终于答应了。

sentences.en: It's a major victory for President Zelensky, both in acquiring some of the last important weapons that he needs for this major offensive that's going to start very soon,
sentences.zh: 这对泽连斯基总统来说是一场重大胜利，不仅获得了他为即将开始的这次重大攻势所需的一些最后的重要武器，

sentences.en: but also obtaining commitments for arms and ammunition.
sentences.zh: 还获得了武器和弹药的承诺。

sentences.en: And this gives his commanders assurances that when this counteroffensive starts,
sentences.zh: 这让他的指挥官们确信，当反攻开始时，

sentences.en: they can be as aggressive as possible because they know more is in the pipeline in the months to come.
sentences.zh: 他们可以尽可能地采取主动，因为他们知道未来几个月还有更多的物资在路上。

sentences.en: And that there is a commitment on the part of Western allies to support him with these major new weapon systeMs.
sentences.zh: 西方盟友承诺支持他获得这些重要的新武器系统。

sentences.en: Okay, so now Zelensky has all this stuff, right, all these weapons, and is really at this point running what amounts to a modern Western-style fighting force, a modern army.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在泽连斯基拥有了所有这些东西，对吧，所有这些武器，而且在这一点上，他实际上正在指挥一支现代化的西方风格作战部队，一支现代化的军队。

sentences.en: And Russia is now up against that modern army, really, for the first time.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯现在确实是第一次面对那支现代化的军队。

sentences.en: I mean, it hasn't seen this before in this war.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在这场战争中它以前没见过这种情况。

sentences.en: That's right,
sentences.zh: 没错，

sentences.en: there'll be tens of thousands of Ukrainian forces that have been trained in special tactics by the United States and other Western allies with much more modern equipment.
sentences.zh: 将有数万名乌克兰军队接受美国和其他西方盟友的特殊战术训练，并配备更现代化的装备。

sentences.en: But the Ukrainians got essentially a crash course in all this.
sentences.zh: 但乌克兰人基本上是速成了这一切。

sentences.en: And so how this actually plays out on the ground is still to be seen.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切在战场上究竟会如何演变，还有待观察。

sentences.en: This is the moment.
sentences.zh: 就是现在。

sentences.en: This is the moment that's been building for months.
sentences.zh: 这是酝酿了几个月的时刻。

sentences.en: And now we'll see whether the Ukrainians can perform, whether they can punch through these Russian defenses and take back territory.
sentences.zh: 现在我们将看看乌克兰人能否表现出色，能否突破这些俄罗斯防线并夺回领土。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之爱及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做DJ时，你每晚都要带着300件最珍贵的收藏品去工作。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this, like, living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最强的队伍。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times, celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》，175年来一直致力于帮助您了解世界，充实度过每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在就访问 nytimes.com/subscribe 订阅，享受特别优惠。

sentences.en: So, Eric, when is this counteroffensive actually supposed to start?
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，这次反攻到底预计什么时候开始？

sentences.en: So some military analysts believe that the early parts of the counteroffensive have already started.
sentences.zh: 一些军事分析人士认为，反攻的初期阶段已经开始了。

sentences.en: We're seeing signs that the Ukrainians are striking supply lines, for instance.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们看到了一些迹象，表明乌克兰人正在打击补给线。

sentences.en: Railroad tracks that would carry troops and supplies to the front lines.
sentences.zh: 那些将部队和物资运送到前线的铁轨。

sentences.en: We've seen attacks on ammunition depots and command posts by the Ukrainians in occupied Crimea,
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到乌克兰人在被占领的克里米亚袭击了弹药库和指挥所，

sentences.en: which would disrupt the Russian ability to thwart the counteroffensive the Ukrainians are planning.
sentences.zh: 这会破坏俄罗斯阻止乌克兰人计划中的反攻的能力。

sentences.en: Then there was this mysterious drone strike over the Kremlin recently.
sentences.zh: 最近克里姆林宫上空还发生了神秘的无人机袭击事件。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Where a couple of small drones, you know, exploded.
sentences.zh: 几架小型无人机，你知道的，爆炸了。

sentences.en: They didn't hurt anybody.
sentences.zh: 它们没有伤害任何人。

sentences.en: They didn't kill anybody.
sentences.zh: 它们没有杀死任何人。

sentences.en: It was the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 当时是半夜。

sentences.en: Putin was not there in the Kremlin.
sentences.zh: 普京当时不在克里姆林宫。

sentences.en: But it raised all sorts of questions about who might be responsible for that.
sentences.zh: 但这引发了各种关于谁可能对此负责的问题。

sentences.en: And then just recently, you've seen some kind of cross-border attacks carried out apparently by Russians working for the Ukrainians inside of Russia itself.
sentences.zh: 就在最近，你还看到了一些跨境袭击，显然是由为乌克兰工作的俄罗斯人在俄罗斯境内实施的。

sentences.en: Crazy.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Like, these are Russians helping Ukrainians?
sentences.zh: 你是说，这些是帮助乌克兰人的俄罗斯人？

sentences.en: Apparently so.
sentences.zh: 显然是这样。

sentences.en: We don't know a lot of details about it, but it's a group called the Free Russian Legion who apparently are carrying out these kind of small-scale attacks,
sentences.zh: 我们不知道太多细节，但这是一个叫“自由俄罗斯军团”的组织，他们显然正在进行这种小规模的袭击，

sentences.en: which is, again, meant to show, hey, we can reach inside your country and strike you, not just hit your military supply lines and, you know, affect the actual battle,
sentences.zh: 这再次旨在表明，嘿，我们可以深入你们的国家打击你们，不仅仅是打击你们的军事补给线，你知道的，影响实际的战斗，

sentences.en: but trying to strike a psychological blow, sabotage-type things, covert operations that are very disruptive and disorienting, perhaps, for the Russians.
sentences.zh: 而是试图进行心理打击，进行破坏活动，进行秘密行动，这对俄罗斯人来说是非常具有破坏性和迷惑性的。

sentences.en: And this is all a preview of what's to come, this pattern of attacks.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都是未来即将发生的事情的预演，这种袭击模式。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: At least it's a pattern of the beginning.
sentences.zh: 至少这是开始的模式。

sentences.en: Again, what you're trying to do in this instance, if you're the Ukrainians, you're trying to confuse the Russians as to what your objective is.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，如果你是乌克兰人，你在这种情况下试图做的是，试图让俄罗斯人对你的目标感到困惑。

sentences.en: Where is this attack going to come?
sentences.zh: 这次袭击会从哪里来？

sentences.en: How is it going to play out?
sentences.zh: 它将如何展开？

sentences.en: So we're going to see feints.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会看到佯攻。

sentences.en: We're going to see misdirection.
sentences.zh: 我们会看到误导。

sentences.en: Or you might see operations starting and stopping.
sentences.zh: 或者你可能会看到行动时断时续。

sentences.en: The Ukrainians are probing for vulnerabilities in these front lines in the south where they're expected to strike hard and look for the areas where they might be able to make a breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰人正在南部前线探测弱点，他们预计会在那里进行猛烈打击，并寻找可能实现突破的区域。

sentences.en: And, Eric, once it actually begins, this counteroffensive, what can we expect it to look like on the ground?
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，一旦反攻真正开始，我们在地面上会看到什么样的情况？

sentences.en: I mean, they have all of these new weapons, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们有所有这些新武器，对吧？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If it works well for the Ukrainians, it should look a lot different than what we've seen in the previous phases of this long war so far.
sentences.zh: 如果这对乌克兰人来说进展顺利，它应该看起来与我们在这场漫长战争的前几个阶段所看到的有很大不同。

sentences.en: If you think about much of this war has been defined by exchanges, almost like a World War I, trench warfare, artillery blasts, back and forth, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果你想想这场战争的大部分时间都是由交火定义的，几乎就像第一次世界大战，堑壕战，炮火轰炸，来来回回，你知道的，

sentences.en: grinding out these very incremental advances on either side.
sentences.zh: 双方都在进行非常缓慢的推进。

sentences.en: This, again, if it works the way the Ukrainians and their Western partners have designed it, is going to move much faster.
sentences.zh: 如果按照乌克兰人和他们的西方伙伴设计的方式进行，这次行动将会快得多。

sentences.en: You're going to have tanks on the ground.
sentences.zh: 你会有地面坦克。

sentences.en: You're going to have armored personnel carriers carrying troops moving through the battlefield supported by artillery fire and synchronizing all of these different kinds of weapons and tactics in a way that they haven't done before.
sentences.zh: 你会有装甲运兵车搭载部队穿过战场，在炮火支援下，以他们以前从未有过的方式协调所有这些不同种类的武器和战术。

sentences.en: And if you can push ahead, you can gain ground much more quickly and break the will of the Russians.
sentences.zh: 如果你能向前推进，你就能更快地获得土地，并摧毁俄罗斯人的意志。

sentences.en: So if it works as intended, this would be a much faster, more modern fight in which Ukraine physically moves through the territory and takes it as it goes.
sentences.zh: 所以如果按预期进行，这将是一场更快、更现代化的战斗，乌克兰将实际穿过领土并随之占领它。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's the goal.
sentences.zh: 这就是目标。

sentences.en: And this is very difficult to do, even for a military as advanced as, say, the American military,
sentences.zh: 这非常困难，即使对于像美国军队这样先进的军队来说也是如此，

sentences.en: particularly when they face the defenses that the Russians have thrown up in front of them.
sentences.zh: 特别是当他们面对俄罗斯人摆在他们面前的防御工事时。

sentences.en: It's a big ask on the part of the Ukrainians, but that's what they've been training to do for the last several months, and we'll see if it works or not.
sentences.zh: 这对乌克兰人来说是一个巨大的要求，但这就是他们过去几个月一直在训练要做的事情，我们将看看它是否有效。

sentences.en: So, Eric, now we come to the eternal and probably unanswerable question, which is, how long can we expect this offensive to last?
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，现在我们来到了一个永恒且可能无法回答的问题，那就是，我们预计这次攻势会持续多久？

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot of things we don't know.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有很多事情我们不知道。

sentences.en: We don't know how well the Russians will defend the ground that they've been digging into for months and months.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道俄罗斯人将如何防守他们已经挖掘了数月的阵地。

sentences.en: They've been laying trenches.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在修筑战壕。

sentences.en: They've been putting down minefields.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在铺设雷区。

sentences.en: They've been putting in things called tank traps.
sentences.zh: 他们一直在设置所谓的坦克陷阱。

sentences.en: So, think of this as, you know, a months-long campaign that's going to go at least through the summer.
sentences.zh: 所以，把这看作是一场至少要持续到整个夏天的数月之久的战役。

sentences.en: And what would success look like for Ukraine coming out of this?
sentences.zh: 那么，乌克兰从中取得什么样的成果才算成功？

sentences.en: So, just in basic terms, remember the Russians now control, still control about 18 percent of Ukrainian territory.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，记住俄罗斯人现在控制着，仍然控制着大约18%的乌克兰领土。

sentences.en: See, the Ukrainians, one of their main goals is just seize back as much of that territory as they can.
sentences.zh: 你看，乌克兰人的主要目标之一就是夺回尽可能多的领土。

sentences.en: And that's important for at least two reasons.
sentences.zh: 这至少有两个原因，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: One is they have to show all these Western donors that have given them all this equipment and money and aid that they can win.
sentences.zh: 一是他们必须向所有给予他们这些装备、资金和援助的西方捐助者证明他们能赢。

sentences.en: They can succeed.
sentences.zh: 他们能成功。

sentences.en: That it was a good investment in the end.
sentences.zh: 最终证明这是一项好的投资。

sentences.en: There was a good investment, right.
sentences.zh: 这是一项好的投资，对吧。

sentences.en: Keep backing us and continue in the future.
sentences.zh: 继续支持我们，并在未来继续下去。

sentences.en: The second other major reason is that they want to put themselves in the best possible position for any kind of negotiated settlement, you know, when and if that happens.
sentences.zh: 第二个主要原因是，他们希望为任何形式的谈判解决方案争取到尽可能好的地位，你知道的，如果那真的发生的话。

sentences.en: That's not really on the cards right now.
sentences.zh: 目前这还不在议程上。

sentences.en: But certainly people are thinking about that and thinking about the impact that a counteroffensive could have on the outcome of such talks.
sentences.zh: 但人们肯定在考虑这一点，并思考反攻可能对这类谈判结果产生的影响。

sentences.en: They'd have a much stronger hand sitting at that negotiating table with, say,
sentences.zh: 如果俄罗斯人只占领了他们国家5%的领土，他们坐在谈判桌前会比俄罗斯人占领18%的领土时拥有更有利的筹码。

sentences.en: the Russians only at 5 percent of their country than they would with the Russians at 18 percent of their country.
sentences.zh: （接上句）

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But the opposite could be true, too.
sentences.zh: 但反之亦然。

sentences.en: Let's say they don't do very well on this counteroffensive.
sentences.zh: 假设他们在这次反攻中表现不佳。

sentences.en: And despite all the weapons that they've been given and despite the fact the Russians have been hobbled by all sorts of problems with their logistics and leadership divisions,
sentences.zh: 尽管他们获得了所有的武器，尽管俄罗斯人因后勤和领导层分歧等各种问题而步履蹒跚，

sentences.en: you know, if the Ukrainians can't take advantage of all that and don't make substantial gains,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果乌克兰人不能利用这一切，没有取得实质性的进展，

sentences.en: there's going to be a lot of pressure on them from the very people who've been supporting them to say, hey, maybe this is the time to basically stop.
sentences.zh: 他们将面临来自那些一直支持他们的人的巨大压力，他们会说，嘿，也许现在是时候基本上停止了。

sentences.en: We'll negotiate a ceasefire, we'll work out terms, but that would leave Russia in control, still a lot of Ukrainian territory, which is going to be hard for Zelensky to stomach.
sentences.zh: 我们将协商停火，我们将商定条款，但这将使俄罗斯仍然控制着大量乌克兰领土，这对泽连斯基来说将很难接受。

sentences.en: So it sounds like the window for the Ukrainians to prove that this aid is working and they can do it is finite, right, is closing.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来乌克兰证明这种援助有效并能做到这一点的窗口期是有限的，对吧，正在关闭。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: All these things that are basically riding on the successful outcome of this counteroffensive are all coming into play in the next several weeks and months.
sentences.zh: 所有这些基本上都取决于这次反攻的成功结果的事情，都将在未来几周和几个月内发挥作用。

sentences.en: And so it really is almost a do-or-die moment for the Ukrainians in their immediate objectives.
sentences.zh: 所以对于乌克兰人来说，在他们眼前的目标上，这确实是一个生死攸关的时刻。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean the war is going to end after this counteroffensive is over, but this is an incredibly important phase of the war up till now.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着战争会在这次反攻结束后结束，但这是迄今为止战争中极其重要的一个阶段。

sentences.en: And why is it so important now, Eric?
sentences.zh: 埃里克，为什么现在这么重要？

sentences.en: Like, what is it about this moment?
sentences.zh: 比如，这个时刻有什么特别之处？

sentences.en: First of all, the funding from the United States, both economic aid and military aid, is set to expire, run out by the end of this summer.
sentences.zh: 首先，来自美国的资金，包括经济援助和军事援助，定于今年夏天结束时到期，用完。

sentences.en: And basically, the counteroffensive will offer a kind of a taste of whatever success or not is made and will help the administration presumably make a case for more money.
sentences.zh: 基本上，反攻将提供一种成功与否的预演，并可能帮助政府为争取更多资金提供理由。

sentences.en: Perhaps even more important is by, you know, late this year, early next year for sure, the election season will be upon us here in the United States.
sentences.zh: 也许更重要的是，到今年晚些时候，肯定到明年年初，美国的选举季就要到了。

sentences.en: And if Biden were to lose the White House, that could very likely mean the end of support for Ukraine, depending on who wins, or at least cutbacks in that support.
sentences.zh: 如果拜登输掉白宫，这很可能意味着对乌克兰支持的终结，取决于谁获胜，或者至少是这种支持的削减。

sentences.en: And the Russians know this.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯人知道这一点。

sentences.en: And it's been part of Putin's strategy.
sentences.zh: 这一直是普京战略的一部分。

sentences.en: He's already started to talk about, I can wait longer than you, the United States, the West can.
sentences.zh: 他已经开始说，我可以比你们，比美国，比西方等得更久。

sentences.en: Your resolve for Ukraine is going to wane.
sentences.zh: 你们对乌克兰的决心将会减弱。

sentences.en: And if there's a change of administrations in Washington, I will benefit.
sentences.zh: 如果华盛顿政府更迭，我将从中受益。

sentences.en: That's Putin's thinking right now.
sentences.zh: 这就是普京现在的想法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, of course, we've seen it time and time again in this war, right, including in Bakhmut.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们在这次战争中一次又一次地看到了这一点，对吧，包括在巴赫穆特。

sentences.en: We are willing to go the distance, and we know you, Western countries, are going to lose interest, turn away, and in the end, that means I win.
sentences.zh: 我们愿意坚持到底，我们知道你们西方国家会失去兴趣，转过身去，最终这意味着我赢了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's why a success and a rather resounding success is so important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么成功，而且是相当响亮的成功如此重要。

sentences.en: Because without that, you not only fail on your military objectives, but also your political objectives become much cloudier, I think, going forward.
sentences.zh: 因为没有这一点，你不仅在军事目标上失败了，而且我认为你的政治目标在未来也会变得更加模糊。

sentences.en: So, Eric, stepping back here for a second, you know, thinking about Zelensky, the really high stakes he's facing right now in this critical phase of the war that's about to begin.
sentences.zh: 那么，埃里克，退一步讲，考虑到泽连斯基，他在即将开始的这个关键战争阶段所面临的极高风险。

sentences.en: How should I understand this moment?
sentences.zh: 我应该如何理解这个时刻？

sentences.en: And thinking back, you know, to the beginning of our conversation, how does Bakhmut, this little city in eastern Ukraine, fit into it, if at all?
sentences.zh: 回想一下我们谈话的开始，巴赫穆特，这个乌克兰东部的小城市，在其中扮演了什么角色，如果有的话？

sentences.en: So, in war, certain places emerge with outside significance, even though they may be small cities like Bakhmut that don't seem to have, apparently,
sentences.zh: 在战争中，某些地方会产生超乎寻常的重要性，即使它们可能像巴赫穆特这样的小城市，看起来似乎并没有，显然，

sentences.en: a lot of strategic significance at all.
sentences.zh: 任何战略意义。

sentences.en: Bakhmut used to be this little town that nobody had ever heard of, and now it's literally on the lips of not just an American president, but Russian president as well.
sentences.zh: 巴赫穆特曾经是一个没人听说过的小镇，现在它不仅挂在美国总统嘴边，也挂在俄罗斯总统嘴边。

sentences.en: So, depending on how this counteroffensive goes, there's a potential that Bakhmut could be seen as an important turning point in the war.
sentences.zh: 所以，取决于这次反攻的进展，巴赫穆特有可能被视为战争中一个重要的转折点。

sentences.en: And here's what I mean.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是这样的。

sentences.en: If the counteroffensive does not go well, and there are going to be a lot of analysts who say Ukraine made a grave mistake in focusing on its efforts, you know,
sentences.zh: 如果反攻进展不顺利，会有很多分析人士说乌克兰在集中精力方面犯了严重的错误，你知道的，

sentences.en: pouring so much manpower and equipment into this lost cause.
sentences.zh: 投入了太多的人力和装备在这场注定失败的事业中。

sentences.en: But if the offensive goes well for the Ukrainians,
sentences.zh: 但如果攻势对乌克兰人来说进展顺利，

sentences.en: Bakhmut could turn out to be a possible potential turning point for how this underdog country could stand up to the giant Russian military.
sentences.zh: 巴赫穆特可能会成为这个弱势国家如何对抗强大的俄罗斯军队的一个潜在转折点。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, in the best-case scenario, Bakhmut could be the marker in our memory of the moment when Ukraine lost the battle but won the war.
sentences.zh: 所以，在最好的情况下，巴赫穆特可能成为我们记忆中的一个标志，标志着乌克兰输掉了战斗但赢得了战争的时刻。

sentences.en: It could be a small place with great importance if the counteroffensive goes well for Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 如果反攻对乌克兰进展顺利，它可能是一个具有重大意义的小地方。

sentences.en: Eric, thank you.
sentences.zh: 埃里克，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的事情。

sentences.en: The Times reports that Governor Ron DeSantis of Florida will announce his highly anticipated entry into the Republican presidential race tonight during a live conversation on Twitter with the platform's owner,
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，佛罗里达州州长罗恩·德桑蒂斯将于今晚在推特上与该平台所有者进行现场对话时，宣布他备受期待地加入共和党总统竞选，

sentences.en: Elon Musk.
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克。

sentences.en: DeSantis will become the seventh Republican to announce his candidacy, a list that now includes former President Donald Trump, former U.N.
sentences.zh: 德桑蒂斯将成为第七位宣布参选的共和党人，名单现在包括前总统唐纳德·特朗普、前联合国大使尼基·黑利，

sentences.en: Ambassador Nikki Haley, and Senator Tim Scott of South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 以及南卡罗来纳州参议员蒂姆·斯科特。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, on Tuesday, Trump's trial on 34 felony counts in connection with a hush money scheme was scheduled for March of 2024,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，周二，特朗普因封口费计划而面临的34项重罪指控的审判被安排在2024年3月，

sentences.en: at the height of the Republican presidential primary.
sentences.zh: 正值共和党总统初选的高峰期。

sentences.en: During a hearing at which the trial date was announced, Trump became visibly angry over the timing, waving his hands and shaking his head.
sentences.zh: 在宣布审判日期的听证会上，特朗普对时间安排表现出明显的愤怒，挥舞着双手并摇头。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们需要完全遮光才能入睡吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they black out to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我指的不是那种喝到断片儿的睡法。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这可是个非常具体的问题。

sentences.zh: 他们是否有过敏或食物不耐受的情况？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
